title: 1968 Alumico burned former Stedmans
description: In 1968, Alumico Building Supply, operated by Brian and Russell Smith, was destroyed by fire. This was one of Hartland’s oldest buildings, originally constructed by George R. Burtt well before 1900, famously built over a tree stump. Burtt initially operated a general store there, with a meeting hall that served the Anglican Church until their new church was built. In 1887, David Keswick took over the store and later sold it to Wendel Tedlie, who opened the Neighbourhood Theatre. After a fire partially damaged the theatre, Tedlie chose not to rebuild. Instead, he sold the property to a group from Saint John in 1938, who remodelled it and opened the modern Capitol Theatre. The Capitol Theatre group eventually relocated further down the street, constructing a new building beside the Post Office, which opened in 1948. The building was sold to the Stedman 5 & 10 chain, which subsequently moved to the J. Clark and Son building in 1966, and the original building was sold to Russell Smith.
